recipes: Soak soya chunks 2 hours ahead. Cooking about 25-30 min (estimated - the chef states no total time; video is 15 min).

200g soya chunks (soaked 2 hrs). Spice powder: 2 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp pepper, 1 tsp cumin, 1.5 tsp fennel, 20g dry coconut - dry roast 2 min, grind, then grind in 3 tsp roasted gram. Also: 3 tbsp groundnut oil, 5-6 dry red chillies, 75g shallots, 2-3 green chillies, curry leaves, 1 onion, 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tomato, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp chilli powder, 3/4 tsp garam masala, salt, coriander leaves.

Dry-roast and grind the spice powder. | Fry red chillies, shallots, green chillies, curry leaves; add onion, then ginger-garlic paste. | Add tomato, turmeric, coriander and chilli powders with 200ml water; cook the masala semi-dry, about 5 min, adding a little oil. | Add strained soya chunks, 2 tsp of the spice powder, coriander leaves; splash of water, flash-cook 2 min on high flame.
Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published 2 Aug 2024). Serve as a starter, evening snack with tea, or with rasam rice.

Bread slices (day-old works best), 1 cup besan/gram flour (250ml), 1 onion, 1 tomato, capsicum, 2 green chillies, coriander leaves, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp ajwain, water, oil.

Mix the chopped vegetables with the spices; crush the ajwain in. | Add besan, then water little by little to a thick batter. | Spread on bread slices; toast on an oiled tawa on medium flame till crisp both sides.
Ingredients from the video description; steps from the video's captions (posted 20 Oct 2026).
2 ripe bananas, 1 egg, 150g jaggery (about 1 cup), 1 cup wheat flour/atta (250ml cup), 1/2 cup boiled and cooled milk, a pinch of salt, a pinch of cooking soda, butter.

Blend banana, egg and jaggery to a creamy mix. | Add wheat flour and milk; mix in salt and cooking soda; thin with a little milk if too thick. | Cook ladles of batter on a buttered tawa, medium flame, covered, till golden both sides.
Ingredients from the description; steps from the video's captions (posted 23 Apr 2026).

Eggs (number not written in the description - shown in the video), 2 cloves garlic, 2 green chillies, 1 onion, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli powder, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp cumin powder, salt, coriander leaves.
Method is shown in the video (not written in the description): spiced onion-chilli mix folded into beaten eggs, cooked as an omelette.
Ingredients from the video description (posted 9 Feb 2026). Serve hot with rice, chapathi or as is.
4 tomatoes, 1/2 cup moong dal, 1/2 cup raw rice, 1 tsp ghee, 1 tsp salt, turmeric, 4 cups water. Tempering: 2 tbsp ghee, cashews, ginger, crushed pepper and cumin, curry leaves, hing.
Method shown in the video: rice and dal cooked with tomato, finished with the ghee tempering.
Ingredients from the video description (posted 31 Mar 2026).

Soak urad dal 1 hour at room temperature + 1 hour refrigerated (mixer method; skip refrigeration if using a stone grinder). Frying 5-6 min per batch. Total ~2.5 hours including soaking, ~30 min active (estimated split; chef states soak and fry times). Video published Jun 18, 2020.

150g good-quality urad dal (wash 5 times to remove white residue), water for grinding (~6 tbsp total), 1/2 tsp hing (asafoetida), little more than 1/2 tsp salt, finely chopped ginger (quantity to taste), chopped green chillies, oil for deep frying. Chef: ginger, green chilli, salt and hing are the only essentials; onion/curry leaves/jeera/red chilli/rice powder/soda are optional variations.

Wash urad dal 5 times; soak 1 hour at room temperature, then refrigerate 1 more hour (mixer method only). | Grind without soaking water: 15 seconds, loosen with a spoon, add 2 tbsp water; repeat grinding and add water 3 times total (~6 tbsp) until a fine, soft, puffy paste. | Transfer to a round bowl; add hing, salt, ginger, green chillies. | Beat well to incorporate air for a fluffy batter. | Fry immediately - do not refrigerate the batter or leave it out more than 30 min or vadas absorb oil. | Shape vadas with a hole in the middle (hole lets oil roast the sides evenly); fry on high flame 5-6 min, flipping, till golden brown. | Drain and serve. Same vada works for vada sambar; soak in hot water and drain before adding curd for dahi vada.

Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published 18 Jun 2020). Chef: stone grinder gives the softest result; urad dal quality is the biggest factor. Batter must be fried within ~30 min of making.

Batter rests 30 minutes; each dosa roasts on slow flame (a few minutes per dosa; exact per-dosa time not stated). Total ~45 min including resting (estimated total; chef states the 30-min rest). Video published Aug 14, 2020.

Measured with one cup/bowl used for everything: 1 cup plain upma rava (sooji) - keep a handful aside for later, 3/4 cup rice flour, 3/4 cup maida, salt, 1 tsp sugar (for caramelized colour), handful chopped cashews, 1 tsp jeera, 1 tsp pepper, finely chopped ginger, green chillies and curry leaves, 4 cups water first + 1 more cup water and the reserved rava after resting, 1/2 tsp hing. Finely chopped onions for the tawa; oil/ghee for roasting (be generous). Optional: idli molaga podi sprinkled on top.

Whisk rava, rice flour, maida, salt, sugar, cashews, jeera, pepper, ginger, green chillies, curry leaves with 4 cups water until lump-free; rest 30 min (rava expands and thickens). | After resting, add the reserved handful of rava, 1/2 tsp hing and 1 more cup water (5 cups total) for a thin pouring consistency. | Heat tawa, spread oil, sprinkle finely chopped onions and roast slightly. | Stir batter well each time, then pour from the corners inward so holes form. | Cook ONE side only on slow flame until crispy bits appear on top (high flame burns the underside and keeps it soft). | Add ghee/oil generously on top; optionally sprinkle molaga podi; roast to golden brown, fold and serve.

Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published 14 Aug 2020). Chef's keys: same cup for all measures, reserved rava added after resting for hotel texture, slow-flame one-side roasting. Pairs with Khara Pudina Chutney (same video).
Khara Pudina Chutney (spicy mint chutney for rava dosa)
About 15-20 min (estimated; no times stated). Chef's own storage note (his claim, not our advice): best eaten same day, keeps max until next day in fridge. Video published Aug 14, 2020.

3 tbsp oil, some jeera, a handful each of chana dal and urad dal (for thickness), a handful of small onions, half a handful of peeled garlic cloves, 4 slit green chillies, 1 1/2 chopped tomatoes, 1/2 tsp turmeric, some hing, half a bunch coriander leaves, 1 full handful pudina (mint) leaves, 2 tbsp tamarind water (from 50g tamarind soaked in hot water), half a grated coconut, salt. Seasoning: 1 tbsp oil, 4 round red chillies, 1/2 tsp mustard, 1/2 tsp urad dal, curry leaves.

Roast jeera, chana dal, urad dal, small onions, garlic and green chillies in oil till golden brown. | Add tomatoes and cook well until no raw smell; add turmeric and hing. | Add coriander and pudina leaves; cook till raw smell goes. | Add tamarind water, cook till raw smell goes, then turn off the gas. | Off heat, mix in grated coconut and salt; cool and grind to a fine paste. | Temper red chillies, mustard, urad dal and curry leaves in oil and pour over the chutney.
Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published 14 Aug 2020). Chef: chana+urad dal make it thick so the rava dosa stays crisp; consume same day or next day max.

Chef states: roast flakes 5-7 min; fry the nuts on slow flame ~10 min; toss the spices 5 min off the heat. Total ~25-30 min (estimated total; chef gives segment times only). Video published Aug 4, 2026.

250g jowar flakes (store-bought, cornflakes-like); 1 tbsp groundnut oil + 1 tbsp oil; a handful of peanuts; ~10 sliced coconut pieces; a handful each of sunflower seeds (or pumpkin/watermelon/muskmelon seeds), almonds, cashews and raisins (dry-fruit mix ~200g total per 250g flakes); chopped green chillies; fresh curry leaves; salt; 1/2 tsp amchur (dry mango) powder; 1/4 tsp turmeric powder; 1 spoon Kashmiri chilli powder; 1 tsp sugar.

Dry-roast the jowar flakes on medium flame 5-7 min patiently till crisp (do not crush them to powder); sieve and set aside. | In the same pan heat the oil on low; roast the peanuts, then the coconut slices (~5 min). | Add the seeds, almonds, cashews and raisins; fry on slow flame ~10 min till crisp. | Add green chillies and curry leaves, then salt, amchur, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli powder and sugar; turn off the gas and toss 5 min on residual heat so the spices coat everything. | Mix in the roasted jowar flakes, cool completely, then store airtight.

From the video's auto-translated English subtitles (published Aug 4, 2026); a few spice quantities were unclear in the translation and are marked approximate. Chef's storage claim: keeps up to 10 days airtight (chef's claim, not independently verified).
Breakfast / lunch / dinner side for set dosa or idly

Chef states: soak chana dal 3 hours; fry vada pieces ~2 min per batch. Masala + gravy ~40-45 min active (estimated; chef gives segment times only). Quantity serves ~6-7 people (chef's estimate). Video published Aug 10, 2020.

Masala paste: 6-8 cloves, 4-5 cinnamon pieces, 6-8 elaichi, 4 slit green chillies, 100g garlic, 60g ginger, 2 tsp saunf (fennel), a handful of roasted gram, 1 tbsp khus khus (poppy seeds), 8 round red chillies, some coriander leaves and pudina, 1/2 coconut grated. Vada: 300g chana dal soaked 3 hours with 6-7 round red chillies and 1 spoon saunf; hing; salt; oil for frying. Gravy: 5 tbsp oil, 2 cinnamon pieces, 2 cloves, 4 elaichi, 1 tsp saunf, 4 round red chillies, a handful of curry leaves, 2 medium onions sliced (up to 4), 1 tsp turmeric powder, 1.5 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 4-5 tumblers water, salt; coriander and curry leaves to finish.

Dry-roast all the masala ingredients, adding the coconut last on residual heat; cool and grind to a fine paste. | Grind the soaked chana dal mixture to a coarse (masala-vada) paste; mix in hing and salt. | Drop shapeless portions into hot oil and fry ~2 min till just brown (three-quarter cooked, not crisp, so they absorb the gravy); strain. | Heat 5 tbsp oil; fry cinnamon, cloves, elaichi, saunf, red chillies and curry leaves; add the onions and roast well. | Add the ground paste, cook briefly, pour 4-5 tumblers water with turmeric, Kashmiri chilli powder and salt; boil till the raw smell goes. | Crumble in the fried vadas, cook 2 min; finish with coriander and curry leaves. The gravy thickens as it rests - thin with hot water when serving.
Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published Aug 10, 2020). Same video as Set Dosa. Tomato can be added after the onions if preferred (chef's note).

Chef states: soak rice and dal 3-4 hours, aval 15 min in buttermilk; grind ~30 min; ferment overnight (8 hours). Per dosa: 2-3 min covered on slow flame (about 5 min for full holes). Batter makes ~15 set dosas (chef states). Video published Aug 10, 2020.

1 kg dosa rice; 150g urad dal; 25-30g (1.5 tsp) fenugreek seeds; 150g aval (poha); buttermilk made from 100g curd beaten with 2 tumblers water; salt. To cook: 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, a little over 1/2 tsp cooking (appam) soda, water to a flowing consistency, oil for the tawa.

Soak the rice, urad dal and fenugreek 3-4 hours; soak the aval in buttermilk 15 min. | Grind the rice-dal fine, then add the strained aval and grind further; add salt, beat well and ferment overnight (~8 hours). | To the batter add sugar, salt, turmeric and cooking soda; thin with water to a flowing consistency slightly thicker than wheat-dosa batter (it should spread on its own when poured). | Pour a ladle on a hot tawa, cover with a lid and cook on slow flame 2-3 min till many holes appear; smear oil and flip briefly for colour. | Always serve as a pair, with vada curry.
Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published Aug 10, 2020). Chef's tip: fewer holes means less soda, or skip the soda and add more aval for softness (chef's guidance).

Chef states: soak basmati 20 min; half-cook the rice ~5 min; dum on the lowest flame 25 min; rest 10 min. Total ~75-90 min (estimated total; chef gives segment times only). Serves ~4 (chef's estimate). Video published Jan 8, 2021.

1/2 kg good basmati rice, washed and soaked 20 min (chef cooks 250g for his pan size; the masala is enough for 1/2 kg); 4 tbsp ghee; 4 cloves, 4 cinnamon pieces, 6 green elaichi, 3 black elaichi, some javitri (mace), 2-3 bay leaves, 1/2 tsp shahi jeera; 3 onions sliced; 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (60:40 garlic:ginger); 4 slit green chillies; 3 medium tomatoes sliced; 1/2 tsp turmeric powder; 1.5 heaped tsp Kashmiri chilli powder; salt; 1/2 tumbler water; mushrooms, washed and halved; 6 tbsp thick beaten curd; 1 full tsp garam masala. For layering: 1/2 bunch pudina, 1/2 bunch coriander, fried onions, roasted cashews, saffron milk, 1/2 tsp kewra water, 3 tbsp ghee.

Boil the soaked rice in plenty of hot water with salt, 1/2 tsp ghee, pudina and coriander for ~5 min till half-cooked; strain. | Heat the ghee and crackle the whole spices; fry the onions till juicy (not brown). | Add the ginger-garlic paste, then the chillies, tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder and salt; pour 1/2 tumbler water and boil. | Add the mushrooms, then the curd; boil 2 min; stir in the garam masala for 1 min. | Layer the half-cooked rice over the masala without mixing; top with pudina, coriander, fried onions, cashews, saffron milk, kewra water and ghee. | Seal the lid (an optional dough seal is the hotel method), place the pan on a dosa tawa and dum on the lowest flame 25 min; rest 10 min before opening.
Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published Jan 8, 2021). The garam masala is from the chef's earlier video on the same channel.
